title: Mammography PACS | High-Resolution Images and Priors
meta: Mammography PACS for large high-resolution images: careful window/level in the browser, prior screening rounds beside today's.
h1: Mammography PACS built for large, detailed images and comparison with the last round.
sub: Mammography images are large and high-resolution, read with careful window/level, and almost always compared with the previous round. AuraPACS stores them on a node in your centre, opens them in a browser at full detail, keeps every prior in the patient's history and shares the report with the patient securely.
meta_ticks: Report to the patient on WhatsApp
whatsapp_text: Hi, we run a mammography unit and would like to discuss AuraPACS.
persona: Owner or radiologist at a diagnostic centre or women's health clinic running a digital mammography unit

paras: A mammography PACS receives the large, high-resolution images from the unit, stores them without loss of detail, presents them for reading with fine window/level control, and keeps every previous round so the radiologist can compare. AuraPACS does this on an on-premise node with a browser viewer, and attaches the signed report to the study for sharing.

Mammography puts two demands on a PACS that other modalities do not. The images are big, so storage and viewing must handle full resolution rather than a downsized copy. And comparison with priors is the norm, so the archive must find last year's study in seconds.

sections.h2: Big images, and a reading that depends on what was seen last time.
sections.lead: Mammography reading is slower and more careful than most, and the workflow around it has to respect that.

items.p: Last year's screening round is on a disc the patient may or may not have kept, so comparison is often impossible.

sections.h2: From the unit to a report the patient can open.

steps.p: The patient is booked once; the entry reaches the mammography worklist.
The technologist selects the patient on the unit; views are captured.
Full-resolution images are sent as DICOM to the node and filed under the patient.
The previous round is found in the patient history and opened beside today's.

A secure link is sent to the patient and referring doctor on WhatsApp.

items.q: Are mammography images stored at full resolution?
items.a: Yes. The node receives whatever the unit sends as DICOM and stores it as received. The browser viewer opens the study at full detail rather than a preview copy.

items.q: Can the radiologist compare with last year's round?
items.a: Yes. Earlier studies are in the patient's searchable history on the node and can be opened alongside the current study in the viewer, with independent window/level.

items.q: Does the viewer support the fine window/level mammography needs?
items.a: The browser viewer provides window/level adjustment on the full-resolution image. Reading-room display hardware and its calibration remain your choice; AuraPACS does not supply monitors. See DICOM viewer.

items.q: How does the patient receive her report?
items.a: By a secure link sent on WhatsApp, which opens the report PDF and, if you choose, the images, without any login. Access is role-based and every view is audited. See WhatsApp report sharing.

items.q: How much storage does mammography need?
items.a: More per study than X-ray or ultrasound, because the images are large. The archive is on your own node and is sized to your annual volume on a call, with an encrypted offsite copy.
